Bula Boys secure 2-0 victory over PNG in MSG Prime Minister’s Cup
item.description: The Fiji Bula Boys have secured an important 2-0 victory over Papua New Guinea in the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup 2026. The Bula Boys went into half-time leading 2-0.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Bula Boys have secured an important 2-0 victory over Papua New Guinea in the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup 2026.

The Bula Boys went into half-time leading 2-0.

Captain Roy Krishna opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the 18th minute at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva, giving Fiji a 1-0 lead.

Six minutes later, Sterling Vasconcellos doubled Fiji’s advantage with a goal in the 24th minute.

Papua New Guinea were unable to find the back of the net in the second half as Fiji held on to secure the 2-0 victory and all three points.

The Bula Boys will now play their final match against New Caledonia at 7pm Wednesday at the HFC Bank Stadium.

item.title: Flying Fijians name extended squad for Japan Test and November tour
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 27/09/2026 The FIJI Water Flying Fijians have named a 68-member extended squad for their upcoming Test against Japan next month, as well as their Northern Tour.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 27/09/2026

The FIJI Water Flying Fijians have named a 68-member extended squad for their upcoming Test against Japan next month, as well as their Northern Tour.

The squad includes 37 forwards and 31 backs.

Some prominent names included in the squad are Peni Ravai, Tevita Ikanivere, Mesake Doge, Isoa Nasilasila, Joseva Tamani, Etonia Waqa, Peceli Yato, Vilive Miramira, Kitione Salawa, Levani Botia, Pita Gus Sowakula, Frank Lomani, Terio Tamani, Caleb Muntz, Jiuta Wainiqolo, Iosefo Masi, Setareki Bituniyata, Vinaya Habosi and Virimi Vakatawa.

Fiji will take on Japan at 5:50pm on Saturday, 24th October.

Looking at Fiji’s matches in November, the Flying Fijians will face France on 8th, followed by Ireland on 15th, before meeting Italy on the 22th in their final match.

item.title: Valetini to start while Canham ruled out for Wallabies Test against Springboks
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 27/09/2026 The Wallabies have named their 23-member team for tonight's Test against world number one South Africa, with Rob Valetini starting at flanker, while lock Josh Canham has been ruled out with a hamstring injury.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 27/09/2026

The Wallabies have named their 23-member team for tonight's Test against world number one South Africa, with Rob Valetini starting at flanker, while lock Josh Canham has been ruled out with a hamstring injury.

Canham was named to start in tonight's match; however, Lukhan Salakaia-Loto will replace him in the starting line-up, with Lachlan Shaw added to the bench.

Head coach Les Kiss has also named 23-year-old Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to make his first start on the wing, where he will team up with Max Jorgensen and Tom Wright.

Hunter Paisami returns to the centres alongside Len Ikitau, while Ryan Lonergan will team up with Ben Donaldson in the halves.

The Wallabies will take on the Springboks at 9:45 tonight at Optus Stadium in Perth.

Fijiana edge Netherlands 20-17 to win WXV title
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 27/09/2026 The Vodafone Fijiana XV have created history, claiming the WXV Global Series Challenger title for the first time after defeating the Netherlands 20-17 in a closely contested match.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 27/09/2026

The Vodafone Fijiana XV have created history, claiming the WXV Global Series Challenger title for the first time after defeating the Netherlands 20-17 in a closely contested match.

The Fijiana got off to a flying start, with tries to Merewairita Neivosa and Ivamere Nabura Rokowati to lead 12-7 at half-time.

The Netherlands came back strongly in the second half, scoring two quick tries through Linde van der Velden and Pleuni Kievit to take a 17-12 lead.

Fiji did not give up, continuing to put pressure on the Netherlands, which resulted in a try to prop Selai Naliva to level the scores at 17-all.

A last-minute penalty gave the Fijians a chance to make history, and Varanisese Qoro stepped up and slotted the three-pointer to seal the win.

Neivosa was awarded the Player of the Match award.
